name: Edward Ball Wakulla Springs State Park
coordinateNote: USGS monitoring location 02327000, rounded to six decimals; spring-area marker, not vehicle entrance.
navigationAddress: 465 Wakulla Park Drive, Wakulla Springs, FL 32327
experience: An enormous spring with a vent about 185 feet deep, a swimming area and wildlife boat trips through ancient cypress swamp. The Florida Geological Survey establishes the vent depth; the park describes manatees and alligators. The deep vent is a geological feature, not the depth or boundary of the designated swimming area. Combine a swim with the riverboat for two distinct experiences.
duration: Plan half a day; boat-ticket timing controls the visit.
cost: Official fee page: $4 solo vehicle or $6 for 2–8 occupants; adult riverboat ticket $8 extra. Rates may change.
access: Park posts 8 a.m.–sundown. Boat tickets require reservations. Do not treat the park's general scuba category as authorization to dive its main spring.

name: FR 33 at FR 38 (Juniper Prairie Road) junction, wilderness trail entrance
coordinateNote: Entrance, parking or campsite coordinates from the November 12, 2026 research.
navigationNote: Drive to the listed entrance; follow the access description on arrival.
experience: A T-junction where gravel FR 38 meets gravel FR 33, with room to park at a marked trail that runs east into the Juniper Prairie Wilderness. The Dyrt pins a free 'Ocala National Forest' dispersed site here, three miles north of Juniper Springs Campground. Quieter and further from highway noise than the first mile of FR 33.
access: No reservation needed. Stay limit: 14 days in a 30-day period Ocala WMA general gun season is Nov 14, 2026 - Jan 10, 2027 in the Pipeline, Hopkins Prairie and Lake Delancy units (Church Lake Unit on the far west edge: Nov 14-22 and Nov 28 - Dec 6). FWC 2026-27 brochure: 'During the general gun season, camping is prohibited, except in designated campgrounds and Juniper Prairie Wilderness.' Forest Service: 'Camping is allowed only in designated campsites during general gun season.' So roadside dispersed camping here is NOT legal on any night of Nov 21 - Dec 8, 2026; it was legal in late October. Deer hunters must wear 500 sq in of fluorescent orange; wear orange yourself if you walk outside a campground. Walk-in tent camping inside the Juniper Prairie Wilderness east of the road stays legal during general gun season, but no vehicles are allowed in the wilderness.

conditions.summary: Sleeping in the car at the roadside is prohibited during general gun season, Nov 14, 2026 - Jan 10, 2027. Legal again from Jan 11, 2027. (source dated read 2026-11-12)
